hints: Look at White's queen on c5 and count what defends the pawn on e4.

items.explain: Na4 attacks the queen on c5 and the knight on c3, which is the only white piece defending the pawn on e4. The knight on a4 is itself loose, attacked by the knight on c3. The engine at depth 16 rates Na4 at least 1.5 pawns above each of Re8, Nbd7 and Bxf3.

feedback_by_move.b6d7: Nbd7 retreats the knight; the engine at depth 16 rates it at least 1.5 pawns below Na4.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Ne2+ (depth 16).
The engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 6 pawns in Black's favour (White's point of view: -600 or lower).
After Ne2 the knight attacks g1, so it is check.
After Ne2+ the white king has exactly one legal move.

axb6 is rated at least 8 pawns below Ne2+ (depth 16).

hints: Black has just taken a bishop with check. Now look at the white king and at your knight on c3.
Black has several captures here: the rook on d1, the bishop on b6, and pawns on a2 and d4. One knight move gives check instead; where can the white king go then?
Ne2+. The king must go to f1, and then the knight on e2 stands on the diagonal between your bishop on c4 and the king.
items.explain: Ne2+ is check, and the white king has exactly one legal move. The engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 6 pawns in Black's favour, although Black has just given up a queen. Taking material at once with Nxd1, axb6 or Bxd4 is rated at least 5 pawns lower.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move. (More than one move is accepted.)

claims.statement: The engine's best move is one of Nc3+, Ng3+, Nf4+, Nxd4+, Nc1+, and all five are rated within 0.8 pawn of the best (depth 16).
The engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 5 pawns in Black's favour (White's point of view: -500 or lower).
At the start the white king on f1 is not attacked: the knight on e2 blocks the bishop on c4.
A white pawn stands on d4, so Nxd4+ is a capture.
After the knight goes to d4, 1 black piece attacks the king on f1. The bishop on c4 gives the check.
After the knight goes to c3, 1 black piece attacks the king on f1. The bishop on c4 gives the check.
After the knight goes to f4, 1 black piece attacks the king on f1. The bishop on c4 gives the check.
After the knight goes to c1, 1 black piece attacks the king on f1. The bishop on c4 gives the check.
After the knight goes to g3, 2 black pieces attack the king on f1. That is a double check.
axb6 is rated at least 0.4 pawn below the best move (depth 16).
Ng1+ is rated at least 8 pawns below the best move (depth 16).
After Ng1+ no black piece defends the knight on g1, so the white king can take it.
After Ng1+ the white king has exactly one legal move: the capture on g1.
After Nxd4+ one black piece, the bishop on c4, attacks d3, so a blocker there can be taken.
After Nxd4+ the white queen has exactly one legal move: the block on d3.
After Nxd4+ the white rook on d1 has exactly one legal move: the block on d3.
After Ng3+ the white queen has no legal move.
After Ng3+ the white rook on d1 has no legal move.

hints: White's king stands on f1. Your bishop on c4 points at it. What is in the way?
Any move of the blocking piece uncovers the bishop's attack. Which of its moves also does something useful?
Look at the white pawn on d4, and at which knight moves attack something or give a second check.
items.explain: The knight on e2 blocks the bishop on c4, so each of these five knight moves uncovers a check. Ng3+ is a double check, since the knight attacks f1 as well. The game went Nxd4+, which also takes a pawn. The engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 5 pawns in Black's favour and rates the five moves within 0.8 pawn of the best. Before you play a discovered check, ask two questions: can the king simply take the piece that moved, and can the line be blocked? Ng1+ fails the first: the white king takes the knight. After Nxd4+ White can block on d3 with the queen or the rook, yet the bishop on c4 attacks d3. After Ng3+ the queen and the rook have no legal move: in a double check only the king can move.

feedback_by_move.a7b6: axb6 takes the bishop that took your queen, and it is the move played in the game at move 23. Here, though, the engine's best move at depth 16 is one of the five knight checks, and it rates axb6 at least 0.4 pawn below the best of them.
feedback_by_move.e2g1: Ng1+ also uncovers the check, but the white king can simply take the knight on g1, which nothing defends. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 8 pawns below the best knight check.
